metadata.title: British Columbia Systems Corporation: life cycle and the continuation of its functions

conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by the source; a year is never 1 January

events.title: Systems Act assented: British Columbia Systems Corporation established to consolidate and coordinate the government’s data processing
events.interpretation_notes: Finance Minister Evan Wolfe described government computing as fragmented; the corporation brought together the medical plan’s installation, Finance’s, two in Energy, Transport and Communications, several smaller centres and about 300 staff, with Victoria as headquarters. It could serve other governments, Crown corporations, universities, municipalities and regional districts, recovering costs by user charges. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: The government announces it will offer all or part of the corporation for sale
events.interpretation_notes: The 1983/84 Public Accounts record that all bids were rejected and the corporation was instead streamlined, with some services privatized. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: Facilities management of the central computer facility contracted to Hi-Tech Systems Ltd., a company of former BC Systems employees, until 30 September 1986
events.interpretation_notes: Recorded in the Public Accounts that followed the 1983 sale offer; the contract’s start date is not given. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: BC OnLine created, managed by BC Systems: electronic access to land titles, personal property security, company registrations and other government databases
events.interpretation_notes: Its operation, commercial development and marketing passed to MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates from 1 May 1999; its accounts are now being moved into the BC Registry application. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: Employees and operating business, all but the general manager, transferred to the Information Technology Services Division of the Information, Science and Technology Agency
events.interpretation_notes: The end of BC Systems’ operating life as a separate Crown corporation; the government’s records schedule names ITSD (and later Workplace Technology Services) as its successor. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: Budget Measures Implementation Act, 1998 provides for the repeal of the System Act and the corporation’s dissolution, to take effect later
events.interpretation_notes: From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: The Province contracts with IBM Canada for mainframe services, subcontracted to ISM-BC (TELUS Enterprise Solutions from 2001)
events.interpretation_notes: Recorded by the Auditor General; ITSD kept responsibility for the mainframe environment’s controls. A contracted provider, not a successor. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: British Columbia Systems Corporation dissolved; its remaining rights, property, assets, obligations and liabilities pass to the Province
events.interpretation_notes: References to the corporation in contracts and other instruments are deemed to refer to the government. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: The former BC Systems role continues inside government: ITSD becomes Common IT Services, then part of Solutions BC (1 April 2003), then Shared Services BC, and its Technology Solutions Division reports to the Office of the Chief Information Officer from December 2011
events.interpretation_notes: A succession of functions, whose scope widened as other services were added; the legal succession is the Province’s. Managed hosting and data centres went to EDS (later HP) Advanced Solutions under a 2009 agreement — a contracted provider, now Advanced Solutions, a DXC Technology Company. From a research summary supplied on 2026-11-12, citing the corporation’s accounts, the Public Accounts, the statutes and government records; those sources were not re-read in this pass.

events.title: Connected Services BC formed in the Ministry of Citizens’ Services, combining ministry information-management and IT branches with the Office of the Chief Information Officer — the strongest present-day continuation of BC Systems’ central IT role
